_meta.note: V2.1 (2026-09-07, owner correction pass): a real quote (UK MOT scenario) exposed three residual reasoning leaks and one bug. (1) General repair knowledge (shocks sometimes replaced in pairs) was silently becoming a case-specific specific_concern, including a predicted future consequence ('could mean a second bill within months') nobody established. (2) Missing documentation of a diagnostic step was still implying the step wasn't performed, and additional findings during inspection were framed as 'opportunistic'. (3) 'OEM vs aftermarket' was framed as inherently a quality claim rather than a comparison variable. Fixed: specific_concerns now requires an explicit 'what positive evidence makes this a concern?' test (added to both the system prompt and the final self-check) - general knowledge, undocumented steps, and additional findings all route to unknowns_that_matter/questions_to_ask instead; future-consequence predictions banned outright; part-type framed as a comparison variable, never a quality hierarchy; second_opinion barred from implying poor foundation via 'undocumented = unfounded'. Also fixed a genuine bug: the model would write '$1,290' in some fields and '£1,290' in others when the free-text repair description used British terms (MOT, tyres) despite the visitor's actual currency being USD - added an explicit CURRENCY rule (use ONLY the given currency for every figure, regional vocabulary in the description is not a currency signal, always attach the symbol) plus a currency reminder at the top of the user prompt and an inconsistent_currency guard prohibition. Verified live on the reported scenario across 3 consecutive calls: specific_concerns went from a false positive (2 concerns) to correctly empty (3/3 runs), currency consistent throughout in all 3 runs, and the model surfaced a genuinely useful NEW catch on its own ('the MOT failure was on one disc but the quote covers all four corners') as an unknown, not an invented diagnosis.

input.whatWentWrong: Not cooling properly, freezer is fine but the fridge side is warm
input.whatTheyToldYou: Technician said the compressor is failing and needs full replacement

output.understanding: Your 6-year-old Whirlpool refrigerator is cooling normally in the freezer but not on the fridge side, and a technician has diagnosed a failing compressor and quoted $450 for full compressor replacement. No itemized document was attached, so the breakdown behind that $450 is unknown.
output.verdict_explanation: The $450 figure is a single total with no breakdown of parts, labor, or fees supplied, so it cannot be meaningfully audited. More importantly, the symptom you described — freezer working, fridge side warm — can have more than one cause, and before approving a major repair like compressor replacement it is worth understanding what testing led to that specific diagnosis. Without knowing what the $450 covers or how the diagnosis was reached, evaluation is limited.

quote_summary.stated_diagnosis: Compressor is failing and needs full replacement

unknowns_that_matter: What diagnostic test or measurement led to the compressor diagnosis — the symptom of a warm fridge with a working freezer can have more than one cause, and knowing what was tested helps you evaluate whether compressor replacement is the right scope.
How the $450 breaks down between parts and labor — without this you cannot compare against another quote or assess whether the total is reasonable for the work described.
Whether a warranty is included on parts, labor, or both, and for how long — this matters significantly for a repair of this cost on a 6-year-old appliance.
Whether the diagnostic or service call fee, if one was charged, is credited toward the repair total or billed separately on top of $450.

repair_vs_replace.assessment: At 6 years old, whether to repair or replace depends on the replacement cost in your market, the overall condition of this unit, and what warranty comes with the repaired compressor — none of which are known yet.
missing_information: Current replacement cost for a comparable refrigerator in your market
Overall condition and reliability history of this unit
What warranty, if any, comes with the repaired compressor
Whether any other components are showing wear that could lead to further repairs

questions_to_ask: What testing or measurement led to the compressor diagnosis — was anything else checked, like the evaporator fan or defrost system?
Can you break down the $450 into parts and labor so I can understand what I am paying for?
What warranty comes with the replacement compressor and the labor?
Is the diagnostic or service call fee already included in the $450, or is it billed separately?
output.what_to_say: Before I approve the repair, I have a few questions. Can you walk me through what you tested or measured that points specifically to the compressor, rather than something like the evaporator fan or defrost system? And can you give me a breakdown of the $450 into parts and labor, along with what warranty would be included? I want to make sure I understand what I am approving before I commit.

second_opinion.reason: Compressor replacement is among the more consequential and costly appliance repairs. A second opinion would confirm the diagnosis and the scope of work before you approve the repair.

input.whatTheyToldYou: They said I need new brake pads, rotors, and calipers on all four wheels

output.understanding: You have a 2018 Honda Civic with 85,000 miles making a grinding noise when braking, and a shop has quoted you $1,800 to replace brake pads, rotors, and calipers on all four wheels. No written document was attached, so the evaluation is based entirely on what you typed.
output.verdict_explanation: The $1,800 total covers a significant scope — pads, rotors, and calipers on all four wheels — but you have no itemization showing what portion is parts versus labor, no information on part quality or warranty, and no documented basis for why all four calipers need replacement rather than just pads and rotors. Without that breakdown, it is not possible to assess whether the price is reasonable or whether the full scope is warranted.

quote_summary.stated_diagnosis: Brake pads, rotors, and calipers needed on all four wheels
quote_summary.proposed_work: Replace brake pads, rotors, and calipers on all four wheels

unknowns_that_matter: Why all four calipers are being replaced is not explained — calipers are a more significant component than pads and rotors, and the quote does not say whether they are leaking, seized, or damaged, or whether replacement is necessary or preventive.
No itemization exists between parts and labor, so there is no way to assess where the $1,800 is going or to compare it against another quote on equal terms.
Part quality is unknown — no information on whether parts are OEM, aftermarket, or remanufactured, and no warranty terms were stated.
Whether the diagnostic fee, if any was charged, is included in the $1,800 or would be added on top is unknown.
questions_to_ask: Can you break the $1,800 into parts and labor separately, and list the parts by brand or part number?
What did you find on inspection that shows all four calipers need to be replaced — were they seized, leaking, or something else?
What warranty comes with the parts and the labor?
Is there a diagnostic fee, and if so, is it included in this $1,800 or separate?
output.what_to_say: Before I approve this, I would like a written breakdown separating parts from labor, with the brand or part number for the calipers, pads, and rotors. What specific condition of the calipers led to the replacement recommendation — are they leaking, stuck, or damaged? And what warranty covers the parts and the work?

second_opinion.reason: Replacing all four calipers is a substantial recommendation on top of pads and rotors. You have no itemization showing how the $1,800 breaks down, and no explanation of why all four calipers need replacement. An independent inspection would let you confirm the diagnosis and scope before committing.

output.safety_note: A grinding noise when braking can indicate significantly worn brake components. Until the brakes are inspected and repaired, avoid high-speed driving and leave extra stopping distance, and if the grinding worsens, braking feels spongy, or the pedal sinks toward the floor, stop driving the vehicle and have it inspected immediately.

input.whatWentWrong: Reinigt nicht richtig, Geschirr kommt mit Essensresten heraus
input.whatTheyToldYou: Der Techniker sagte: "Die Umwälzpumpe ist defekt und muss komplett ersetzt werden"

output.understanding: Ihr Bosch-Geschirrspüler (ca. 4 Jahre alt) reinigt nicht mehr richtig, und der Techniker hat eine defekte Umwälzpumpe diagnostiziert sowie deren Austausch für insgesamt €280 angeboten. Es liegt kein Dokument vor, und der genaue Aufschluss von Teile- und Arbeitskosten ist nicht bekannt.
output.verdict_explanation: Der Gesamtpreis von €280 ist genannt, aber es ist nicht klar, wie sich dieser Betrag auf Ersatzteil und Arbeitszeit aufteilt. Ebenso fehlen Angaben dazu, auf welchem Befund die Diagnose basiert und ob eine Garantie auf die Reparatur gegeben wird. Ohne diese Informationen lässt sich das Angebot nur schwer einschätzen oder mit einem Vergleichsangebot abwägen.
unknowns_that_matter: Aufschluss des Preises: Wie viel entfällt auf das Ersatzteil (Umwälzpumpe) und wie viel auf die Arbeitszeit? Das ist nötig, um das Angebot sinnvoll einzuschätzen oder zu vergleichen.
Grundlage der Diagnose: Das Angebot nennt keinen Befund oder Messvorgang, der zur Diagnose geführt hat. Es ist nicht bekannt, welche Prüfung durchgeführt wurde.
Garantie auf Reparatur und Ersatzteil: Es ist nicht bekannt, ob und wie lange auf die Reparatur oder das eingebaute Teil Garantie gewährt wird.
Teileangabe: OEM-Teil oder Nachbauteil? Neue oder aufbereitete Pumpe? Das beeinflusst die Vergleichbarkeit mit einem Zweitangebot.

repair_vs_replace.assessment: Ohne den aktuellen Kaufpreis eines vergleichbaren Bosch-Geschirrspülers und eine Einschätzung des Gesamtzustands des Geräts lässt sich eine fundierte Abwägung zwischen Reparatur und Neukauf hier nicht treffen.
missing_information: Gesamtzustand und bisherige Zuverlässigkeit des Geräts
Ob das Gerät noch unter gesetzlicher Gewährleistung steht (2 Jahre ab Kauf)

questions_to_ask: Können Sie mir den Preis aufschlüsseln: Was kostet das Ersatzteil, was die Arbeitszeit?
Worauf basiert die Diagnose, dass die Umwälzpumpe defekt ist? Wurde eine Messung oder ein konkreter Befund festgestellt?
Handelt es sich um ein Original-Bosch-Ersatzteil oder ein Nachbauteil, und ist es neu oder aufbereitet?
Gibt es eine Garantie auf die Reparatur und das eingebaute Teil, und wenn ja, für wie lange?
output.what_to_say: Vielen Dank für das Angebot. Bevor ich zustimme, hätte ich noch ein paar Fragen: Können Sie mir den Betrag von €280 aufschlüsseln, also Ersatzteil und Arbeitszeit separat ausweisen? Außerdem würde ich gern wissen, wie die Diagnose gestellt wurde und ob auf die Reparatur eine Garantie gegeben wird.

second_opinion.reason: Da keine Aufschlüsselung des Preises und keine dokumentierte Diagnosegrundlage vorliegen, kann ein zweites Angebot helfen, den Preis einzuordnen und die Diagnose zu überprüfen.

output.understanding: You have a written estimate from Metro Auto Repair for a 2018 Honda Civic with a grinding noise when braking. The estimate totals $1,708.00 and proposes replacing all four brake pads, all four rotors, and all four calipers.

However, the 24-hour approval deadline is a concrete pressure tactic written into the quote itself, and the quote contains no warranty terms, no documentation of what inspection or measurement led to recommending four new calipers, and no tax or fees line — all of which are material gaps on a $1,708.00 brake job that includes the most expensive components on this estimate.

quote_summary.stated_diagnosis: Grinding noise when braking — no specific diagnostic finding documented
quote_summary.proposed_work: Replace front and rear brake pads, front and rear rotors (2 each), front and rear calipers (2 each)

arithmetic_check.assessment: The seven line items sum to exactly $1,708.00, matching the stated total — no arithmetic discrepancy.

specific_concerns.concern: The quote includes a written 24-hour deadline to approve: 'Please approve within 24 hours to lock in this price.'
specific_concerns.why_it_matters: A written time-pressure clause on a brake repair of this scope limits your ability to get a second opinion or ask follow-up questions — and brakes are a category where getting things right matters for your safety.

specific_concerns.concern: The quote does not include warranty terms for the parts or labor.
specific_concerns.why_it_matters: On a $1,708.00 job replacing six major brake components, you have nothing in writing about what happens if a part fails or the work needs to be redone.

unknowns_that_matter: What inspection or measurement led to recommending all four calipers? Calipers are the most expensive items on this estimate ($660.00 combined). The quote does not document the finding, so you cannot yet judge whether the recommendation fits what was actually observed.

output.what_to_say: I want to understand the caliper recommendation before I approve this. Can you tell me what you found on inspection that showed all four calipers need replacing? I also did not see any warranty terms on the estimate — can you put that in writing before I sign off? And I need a bit more time than 24 hours to look this over, so I will get back to you.

second_opinion.reason: The estimate includes a pressure deadline, the caliper recommendation lacks documented findings to evaluate, and the caliper line items account for $660.00 of the total — enough that an independent inspection of the brake system would let you compare the findings and recommendations against what Metro is proposing.

output.safety_note: Until the repair is done or inspected by a qualified technician, pay attention to how the brakes feel and respond. If the grinding worsens, the pedal becomes soft or spongy, or braking feels significantly reduced, do not drive the vehicle and have it inspected immediately.
